title: Fortnightly cetuximab + FOLFIRI

agents.name: Cetuximab
agents.mechanism: Blocks growth messages at the cell surface
agents.explanation: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks growth messages. In bowel cancer, a validated RAS wild-type result helps identify whether this approach is suitable. In head-and-neck cancer, weekly cetuximab may be combined with radiotherapy under a separate treatment plan. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care.
agents.watch: Report rash or sore nails early. Tell the nurse immediately about infusion symptoms. Eye pain, new breathing problems or severe diarrhoea need prompt advice. Blood tests check minerals during treatment and for two months afterwards.
risks: Rash, dry skin, cracks and sore nails
Infusion reaction; rare serious lung or skin effects

agents.name: Irinotecan
agents.explanation: The body converts irinotecan into SN-38. This traps an enzyme called topoisomerase I while DNA is being copied, causing damage that can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal bowel and blood-forming cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about cramps, sweating or diarrhoea during the infusion. Diarrhoea starting later needs the separate written treatment and contact plan.
risks: Rare serious lung or allergic reactions

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself.
agents.watch: The combined treatment can increase mouth soreness and diarrhoea. Report these promptly. Rare allergic reactions can occur.

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
agents.watch: Diarrhoea, mouth sores and skin soreness may become serious. Chest pain during the pump infusion needs emergency assessment. Unexpected severe early toxicity can occur even after DPD testing.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity

questions.a: This combination is used for RAS wild-type bowel cancer that has spread. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates to understand the cycle?
questions.a: No. The graph explains a general pattern. Your hospital arranges appointments; the guide and its safety information are available without entering anything.

questions.q: Will I have a pump at home?
questions.a: Confirm port/PICC preparation, pump connection, home care and professional disconnection around Day 3.

questions.q: What happens if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team checks the cause and may delay, reduce, change or stop one medicine. Ask which component changes and when you should next attend; do not restart yourself.

questions.q: How will I know whether it is helping?
questions.a: Scans, symptoms and clinical review assess benefit. A rash, side effect or good day alone cannot show whether the cancer is responding.
This NCCP regimen does not contain a routine radiotherapy course. If radiation is recommended separately, ask whether it is before, during or after these medicines.

questions.q: What about fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding?
questions.a: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. Ask for the contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine; the whole regimen may require longer precautions than one medicine alone.
RAS testing selects cetuximab treatment in colorectal cancer. It is not the selection test for the separate head-and-neck radiotherapy indication. Confirm the cancer-specific plan with your team.

phases_note: This is a general explanation, not an appointment calendar. Delays or changes are decided by your team. Each medicine can need a different change.
timeline_note: NCCP defines the treatment days. Symptom bands are broad educational guidance; reactions can occur on any day, and cumulative effects may continue between cycles.
safety_note: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell require immediate contact. Serious symptoms override any timeline or diary.
teachback: Can you explain which visits are planned, whether a pump is involved, and which symptoms mean you should call today? No dates or symptom scores are needed to use this guide.
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, serious and lasting risks, fertility/pregnancy precautions and the contact plan. Confirm RAS selection for colorectal treatment, infusion premedication, skin care and post-treatment mineral checks. Explain DPD testing and the exact pump schedule. Explain early and delayed diarrhoea separately.
urgent_extra: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly. Call for line pain, swelling, leakage or unexpected pump progress.

chapters.title: Your treatment aim
chapters.intro: The setting changes what benefit means.

items.title: Why this option?
items.text: This combination is used for RAS wild-type bowel cancer that has spread. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

items.title: A plan that can change
items.text: Ask whether the aim is to reduce recurrence risk, control cancer, relieve symptoms or support a local treatment. Your preferences and priorities matter.

items.title: Blood tests and medicines
items.text: Review blood counts, kidney/liver tests, symptoms, allergies and all medicines and supplements. Confirm DPD testing before fluorouracil. Kidney impairment can affect uracil-based DPD testing interpretation. Tell the team about red-meat allergy or tick bites before cetuximab because these can be associated with infusion-reaction risk.

items.title: Preparing access
items.text: Confirm port/PICC preparation, pump connection, home care and professional disconnection around Day 3.

chapters.title: Symptoms in context
chapters.intro: Report what changed and how it affects you.

items.title: When to call
items.text: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly. Call for line pain, swelling, leakage or unexpected pump progress.

items.title: Bowel symptoms
items.text: Irinotecan can cause early cramps/sweating during infusion and delayed diarrhoea after 24 hours. You need separate instructions for each. Follow your written rescue plan. Fever, blood, severe pain, reduced urine or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

items.title: Skin or nerve changes
items.text: Start the prescribed skin-care plan early, use moisturiser and sun protection, and report painful or infected skin or nails. Keep mineral blood-test appointments during treatment and for two months after cetuximab.

items.title: Food, activity and practical help
items.text: Use prescribed anti-sickness medicines, pace activities and ask for nutritional, emotional or practical support.

items.title: Pregnancy and fertility
items.text: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. Ask for the contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine; the whole regimen may require longer precautions than one medicine alone.

chapters.title: Visits and treatment sequence
chapters.intro: Know which steps happen in the clinic and at home.

items.title: The exact delivery plan
items.text: Cetuximab on Day 1. Day 1: irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump; planned disconnection around Day 3. A repeating 14-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan.

items.title: Radiotherapy relationship
items.text: This NCCP regimen does not contain a routine radiotherapy course. If radiation is recommended separately, ask whether it is before, during or after these medicines.

items.title: Symptoms and monitoring
items.text: Continue the cetuximab skin plan and mineral checks for two months after the last dose. Ask which medicines to continue, when to seek help and how response will be assessed.

items.title: Next decisions
items.text: The team reviews benefit, side effects and your priorities. Supportive and palliative care can help alongside active treatment. Ask for a clear next-step and contact plan.

day_groups.title: Treatment and checks
day_groups.body: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and your prescription before treatment. Premedicines and observation are part of cetuximab visits.
day_groups.action: Know the contact number and the next planned visit.

day_groups.title: Pump completion
day_groups.body: Keep the arranged professional pump-disconnection appointment. Do not adjust, reconnect or remove it yourself.
day_groups.action: Call early for symptoms; do not wait for the next appointment.

day_groups.title: Recovery and the next review
day_groups.body: The team uses symptoms, tests and your priorities to decide what happens next.
day_groups.action: Bring questions and a symptom record if useful; this is optional.

evidence.title: CRYSTAL extended RAS analysis
evidence.intro: The cancer setting, previous treatments and schedule affect whether these results apply.
evidence.population: Extended RAS analysis of first-line cetuximab plus FOLFIRI versus FOLFIRI in metastatic colorectal cancer.
evidence.interpretation: RAS wild-type tumours showed benefit in survival, progression and response; tumours with other RAS mutations did not. This was a retrospective biomarker analysis of a weekly-cetuximab trial. It does not provide a personalised forecast or establish every later-line or fortnightly schedule.

chronology_notes.title: Your planned visits
chronology_notes.text: Cetuximab on Day 1. Day 1: irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump; planned disconnection around Day 3. A repeating 14-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan.

chronology_notes.title: No guaranteed safe days
chronology_notes.text: An infection, reaction or other urgent problem can occur at any time. The graph does not predict a personal low point.

chronology_notes.title: Care continues
chronology_notes.text: Continue the skin-care plan and mineral checks arranged after cetuximab. Ask which medicines to continue and when your next review is planned.

anatomy: Eye pain or new visual change needs prompt advice.
Pain or ulcers affecting eating or drinking need advice.
New breathing difficulty requires prompt assessment.
New chest pain needs urgent assessment.
Diarrhoea, increased stoma output or dehydration: call early.
Report painful rash, cracks or infected skin early.
Fever, shivers or sudden illness: contact oncology immediately.
Pain, swelling, leakage or a loose connection needs immediate advice.
